findings.text: no assertion distinguishes the closed route from the routed one: both new parametrisations compare values only, and replacing _sloped_field_closed's body with _sloped_field's leaves the gate green at 285 passed, because the two routes agree to 1e-10 by design; the node's deliverable is not the agreement but the closed evaluation of R, so guard it by making SheetFlux._root_term or _azimuth_rule raise and requiring closed=True to still return the reference values.

the agreement assertion is circular for the A term: sheet.py:509 and :416 both call _arsinh_gradient, so the comparison can only detect a discrepancy in the R block, while the fragment at docs/evidence/fragments/iron-core-magnetisation/icm-closed-field.html presents the end-by-end triple agreement as the evidence that the split is right; say in the test's docstring that A is shared by construction so the agreement is R's alone.

_closed_gradient re-imports jax and jax.numpy at :520 and :526 although both are already bound at module scope (:520 imports jax and .numpy as jnp at :66-67); only nova.jax.config has an import-cycle reason to be local, so the other two lines are noise that reads as if the module could be imported without jax.

_complete_kind_traced is a jax-differentiability adapter for nova.biot.completeelliptic.complete_kind placed in sheet.py rather than beside its owner, so a second consumer needing a traced complete kind must either import it from a private name in an unrelated module or fork it; move it to completeelliptic.py next to complete_kind and _complete_kind_tangent.

closed=True is silently ignored on a flat sheet because the flat branch is tested first; a caller using the flag as an independent check on a flat conic gets the graded route back with no indication, so either refuse the combination or document it in field()'s docstring.

each closed evaluation calls configure_dtypes and runs jax.value_and_grad over an un-jitted descent, costing about 1.2 s per field evaluation against the routed route's tens of milliseconds, which is what took the gate from 6.7 s to 97.9 s; acceptable for a verification route but it makes closed=True unusable for anything but spot checks, so record the cost beside the flag.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit from e64fafe02 to b7de63499: two wip commits build and then a feat commit converges the closed-form path (20ee343c9), with three docs commits recording the diagnosis and one commit recording the landed result; the net change is +182/-41 in sheet.py, +39 in tests, and the fragment.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done_when asks for B_R and B_Z within 1e-10 of the reference over the twelve fixed targets at pi/8, pi/4 and 3pi/8 and agreement with the semi-analytic field to 1e-10; tests/test_edge_sheet.py:49 SLOPED_PARAMS is 3 slopes x 4 distances x 3 stations = 12 targets per slope, and :243 / :254 assert exactly that measure at the gate's log.
item_verdicts.goal: the node goal asks for the sloped field H_l of Part II (eqs 19 and 23a) in closed form beside the landed semi-analytic field; sheet.py:509-570 lands it as a new evaluation path with closed=True on field() and sheet_field(), and the landed route is left intact rather than replaced.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it names the seven commits, records the gate as 285 passed EXIT=0, the baseline arm as 213 passed, the declared mutation and its red log at negative-control.log, and names the gate-final.log on disk.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the reviewed manifest declares nova/biot/sheet.py, tests/test_edge_sheet.py, docs/evidence/fragments/.../icm-closed-field.html and the figures directory; every path in the diff is inside that set and the untouched figures path carries no requirement this node's goal implies

justifications.durability: tests/test_edge_sheet.py:243 and :254 both redden under the declared sign flip (negative-control.log, 72 failed EXIT=1), but neither can redden if the closed route is replaced by the routed one, so the 'closed form' property the node exists to deliver has no guard.
justifications.evidence: gate-final.log ends '285 passed' EXIT=0 at revision 20ee343c9, whose sheet.py is byte-identical to the reviewed head, and regression-existing.log ends '213 passed' EXIT=0; the per-slope worst errors quoted in the fragment are recorded verbatim in probe/field2.log.
justifications.fit: nova/biot/sheet.py:520-526 re-imports jax and jax.numpy already bound at :66-67, and :552 repeats the ends tuple and MU0 scaling of :484 verbatim, against the module family's practice of a lazy jax import inside the function (nova/biot/greens.py:158).
justifications.goal_fidelity: nova/biot/sheet.py:552 _sloped_field_closed evaluates the sloped sheet field from the closed-form R block and its own forward-mode tangents, reachable via field(closed=True) at :593 and sheet_field(closed=True) at :707, beside the untouched graded route.
justifications.reuse: the addition extends the owner: R is formed by completeelliptic.complete_kind and differentiated by completeelliptic._complete_kind_tangent (:589), the same private recurrence nova/biot/elliptic.py:1313 already imports, and no existing jax-differentiable wrapper for the complete kinds exists in the repository.
justifications.scope_discipline: the diff over e64fafe02..b7de63499 touches only nova/biot/sheet.py, tests/test_edge_sheet.py and docs/evidence/fragments/iron-core-magnetisation/icm-closed-field.html, all inside the declared write paths, and the _divide rewrite is consumed by the reduction at sheet.py:313 rather than left standing.
